title: Year four close
hook: a year with thinkers and schools

segments.voice: Yesterday, ahead: the sources read slowly, the poets, a practice of your own. Your line was the summit. Did you circle the one thing to carry? Today the year of thinkers and schools closes. Day one thousand four hundred twenty-six.

Like water. My attempt. Look as if for the first time. Go to the woods. Solid and light. Thank you. Those were the lines that closed each stretch of this year: the Tao Te Ching, Montaigne, Emerson, Thoreau, the science, and the tour of the world's schools. Read in a row, they sound less like conclusions and more like directions for a walk. Soften. Try. Look. Get outside. Keep what's sure, hold the rest loosely. Say thank you on the way out. Today the year ends, and the first book we opened has one more word for the road.
screen: `LIKE WATER. MY ATTEMPT. LOOK.` → `THE WOODS. SOLID AND LIGHT. THANK YOU.` → `DIRECTIONS FOR A WALK.`

segments.voice: First, four companions, read slowly. Lao Tzu, whose book begins by admitting that words fall short. Montaigne, who wrote about himself in pieces this year called attempts. Emerson, who asked us to look as if for the first time. Thoreau, who went to live by a pond to see what life had to teach. None of them asked to be obeyed. Each one walked beside us for a while and then let us go. Second, science, told honestly. Attention, habit and compassion can grow, the studies said, and they said it modestly. So the year's rule was simple: keep what's solid, hold the rest lightly. Third, the world's schools, never ranked. Zen halls and Sufi circles, Jewish study pairs and Quaker silence, Hindu chant and Sikh dawn prayer, Chinese parks at sunrise. Each was met in its own words. This last week asked what drew you, what doesn't fit, and what you actually do. Fourth, water, one more time. The Tao Te Ching, in its eighth chapter, says the highest good is like water. Water benefits everything and doesn't contend. It settles in the low places people look down on. Elsewhere the book adds that nothing is softer than water, yet nothing does better against what is hard. Watch any stream: the water doesn't fight the stone; it goes around. That was the first book of the year, and it's a fair picture of how to walk out of it. Not racing to the top. Not standing still. Moving on, steadily and low, finding a way around what's in the way.
screen: `FOUR COMPANIONS, READ SLOWLY.` · `SCIENCE, TOLD HONESTLY.` · `THE SCHOOLS, NEVER RANKED.` · `WATER, ONE MORE TIME.` · then, large: `ON TOWARD THE TOP.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: walk slowly, like water. If you can stand and move, walk a room or a hallway at half your usual speed. Let your path bend around what's there, a chair, a doorframe, a corner, without pushing anything aside. Let each step settle before the next. If walking isn't possible right now, let your breath move like water instead, in and out, never forced, or trace a slow, winding path with one hand. Nowhere to arrive. Just moving on, low and steady. If you pray, you can walk with a prayer. The bell holds the time.
Year four close. A year with thinkers and schools: four companions read slowly, science told honestly, and the world's ways of practice, each in its own words. Today's word.

Your line: on toward the top. Tonight, write the one line from this year you most want to carry, and put it where you'll see it when tomorrow's reading begins. Day one thousand four hundred twenty-six.

howItsDone: Some people close a year of study with a slow walk, recalling what they read and choosing one line to carry into the next year; some traditions keep a walking meditation of their own.

original.note: Chinese dao, the way: the word the Tao Te Ching opens with, and the book this year began with.

notes: Tao Te Ching 8 is paraphrased (Legge 1891 not quoted). The line about water going around the stone and the stone changing over time is an everyday picture in the spirit of chapters 8 and 78, not a paraphrase of chapter 8 itself; confirm the framing or cut.
The hook's six lines are the carries of the year's block closes (1144 like water, 1184 my attempt, 1219 look as if for the first time, 1261 go to the woods, 1351 solid and light, 1419 thank you).
'A Frenchman who ... called each piece an attempt' rests on the year's own Montaigne block (carry 'my attempt'); confirm the gloss of essai as 'attempt'.
Original 道 (dao) opens Tao Te Ching 1 (道可道); confirm pronunciation guide 'DOW'.
The practice offers a non-walking alternative for listeners who can't walk.

Editor pass: the four companions are now named instead of described in the words day 1420 had just used ('an old Chinese book of short chapters'); cut 'in Concord' and 'his neighbor' (claims rule) and tied Emerson to his own block's carry; the water-wears-the-stone line, which is not in chapter 8, is now a chapter 78 paraphrase plus an everyday stream picture, with chapter 78 cited. howItsDone softened from 'several traditions' to 'some traditions'.
